get.description: Retrieve the JSON Schema and fulfillment state for a requirement or a requirement set. Clients can determine from a single GET whether it is still pending or has already been fulfilled. An ar_ id evaluates a single requirement; an ars_ id returns the schema composed from every member requirement (shared fields deduplicated, member ids never included) and reports fulfilled only once every member is.

post.description: Submit answers for a requirement, or jointly for every member of a requirement set. The payload is merged into any previously stored answers and the cumulative result is evaluated against the resolved (ar_) or composed (ars_) schema. When the cumulative answers satisfy the whole schema the requirement/set is fulfilled ("fulfilled"); otherwise the submission is persisted and it stays "in_progress", returning the field IDs still outstanding. A field that is submitted but empty/invalid returns a 400 with per-field error details (AnswerValidationFailedError); a field ID not present in the schema returns a 400 (UnknownFieldsError). A required field simply not yet submitted is not an error. An ar_ id that is itself a member of a requirement set cannot be submitted individually — it returns 409 requirement_set_submission_required, naming the ars_ id to submit through instead; that ars_ id then dispatches straight to the joint submission. A file field's answer is an array of file IDs from POST /files; each submitted ID is looked up with the caller's own token, and a file the caller cannot see, or that does not match the field's accepted types or size limit, returns a 400 field error (error_type file_not_found, file_type_not_accepted or file_too_large). If files cannot be checked, the submission returns 503 and nothing is saved; it is safe to retry.

answers.description: A key-value map of field IDs to answer values.
